evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/voice_webhooks.rs:757 — the mounted public /api/v1/webhooks/voice/alexa receiver reads the Signature header into _signature and discards it; verify_alexa_signature only checks the cert-URL string format and a 150s timestamp (both attacker-controllable, no nonce) then returns Ok, so no cryptographic signature verification ever runs despite the docstring/INVALID_SIGNATURE response claiming otherwise, allowing request forgery/replay against the voice-command processor.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/voice_webhooks.rs:870 — the mounted /api/v1/webhooks/voice/google receiver's verify_google_request never verifies the Google-Assistant signature or the bearer JWT (it only checks that the token splits into three dot-separated parts and logs the signature length), so the webhook accepts unauthenticated/forged requests with no real provider-authenticity check.

routes/reports.rs:1801 — get_execution_download_url returns a download URL pointing at /api/v1/reports/files/{file_key}, but no route with that path is registered anywhere in api-server/src (only /executions/{id}/download exists), so every completed-report download link 404s and users cannot retrieve generated reports.
